Fetal monitoring findings (recurrent variable decelerations) and maternal hemodynamic instability (tachycardia, hypotension) further corroborate acute intra-abdominal catastrophe. While fibrinogen, lactate, and repeat labs are pending, they are *prognostic and management-guiding*, not *diagnostic* — uterine rupture is a clinical-radiological diagnosis. At Turn 15/16, delay for further data would be unsafe and inconsistent with standard obstetric emergency protocols. No red-flag alternative is better supported; abruption lacks retroplacental clot or persistent contractions, and other differentials are excluded by imaging and context.

[DECISION] PASS
